EQUITY: HEALTH CARE & PHARMACEUTICALS
Acquiring peptide CDMO company (PolyPeptide) Quick Note

Samsung Biologics (SB) on 20 July announced to acquire PolyPeptide Group AG (PPGN) (PPGN SW, Not rated; market cap USD1.7bn), a peptide CDMO company. SB plans to secure a \(100\%\) stake through a tender offer, with total deal value amounting KRW2.7tn. This acquisition represents SB's strategic expansion beyond its antibody contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) capabilities into the peptide CDMO market. We regard SB's key strategic rationale as it could capture the rapidly growing outsourcing demand for GLP-1 peptide manufacturing.

PPGN recorded revenue of EUR236.6bn (+41.6% y-y) in 1H26 with EBITDA margin of 20.7%. The company guided for 2026E revenue growth of 25-30% y-y and high-teens EBITDA margin. Based on PPGN's record (PPGN is participating in one-third of global peptide Phase III trials) and solvent reduction technology, the company has secured contracts with many of the global top 20 big pharmas, to our knowledge.
Total deal value of KRW2.7tn, assuming 100% stake acquisition

- On 20 July, SB announced its plans to acquire \(100\%\) of PPGN at CHF44.31/share, implying an equity value of CHF1.46bn (KRW2.7tn). The acquisition will be financed through a combination of existing cash (KRW1.6tn of cash, cash & equivalent, as of 1Q26), future operating cash flow, and debt while management indicated that equity financing could be a potential option.

- Prior to the launch of the tender offer, Draupnir Holding B.V. (unlisted), PolyPeptide's controlling shareholder with 55.6% interest, irrevocably committed to tendering its entire stake. As such, SB has secured control over the majority of the shares. Completion of the transaction is conditional upon SB acquiring at least two-thirds (66.7%) of the voting rights through the tender offer. The tender offer will be launched by end-August 2026 and continue for ~2 months.
Our thoughts – capturing a share of growing GLP-1 market at 2026E EV/EBITDA of 19.1x

We view the acquisition as strategically attractive, EPS accretive, and financially reasonable. At an implied 19.1x 2026E EV/EBITDA (source: Bloomberg; peers such as Lonza [LONN SW, Not rated] and Bachem [BANB SW, Not rated] both trade at EV/EBITDA of 18.6x – both have no M&A premium), PolyPeptide offers manufacturing platform across Europe (including Sweden, Belgium, France) and the US (California) and operational synergy with SB in the following way: 1) revenue synergies include cross-selling to non-overlapping customer bases and capturing growth in the expanding GLP-1 peptide market, where PolyPeptide leads with the largest Phase III pipeline among CDMOs; 2) cost synergies emerge from enhanced purchasing power and integrating SB's automation with PolyPeptide's peptide expertise; and 3) strategic synergies transform SB from a single antibody CDMO into a diversified platform.
Global GLP-1 RAs – The bonanza would continue (link; 9 July 2026)

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have been the poster child of global healthcare in recent years. Tirzepatide and semaglutide, the two blockbuster GLP-1 RAs, overtook pembrolizumab (a PD-1 inhibitor for the treatment of various types of cancer) in 2025 to become the global No.1 and No.2 best-selling medications, respectively, as per BioSpace data. Eli Lilly (LLY US, not rated), the company behind tirzepatide, is the first pharmaceutical company to reach a USD1tn market cap. PolyPeptide Group history

PolyPeptide Group is a leading peptide active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) CDMO, specializing in the development and commercial manufacturing of therapeutic peptides. The company serves global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across metabolic diseases (including GLP-1 therapies), oncology, endocrinology. PolyPeptide originated as the peptide manufacturing division of Ferring Pharmaceuticals (unlisted) in 1952. In 1996, Ferring separated the manufacturing business into an independent CDMO. PolyPeptide was listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange in 2021.

Definition of NOM Group's equity research rating system and sectors

The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, subject to limited management discretion. An analyst's target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.
STOCKS

A rating of 'Buy', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to outperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Neutral', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to perform in line with the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Reduce', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to underperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Suspended', indicates that the rating, target price and estimates have been suspended temporarily to comply with applicable regulations and/or firm policies. Securities and/or companies that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 'No rating' are not in regular research coverage. Investors should not expect continuing or additional information from NOM relating to such securities and/or companies.
